news.headline: A Thumb-Sized Mouse Makes a Comeback
news.body: The Pacific pocket mouse is one of the smallest mammals in North America — shorter than a human thumb! Scientists once thought it was gone forever, but San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance has released about 500 of the tiny mice back into the wild in California. The team even runs a kind of "mouse boot camp" so the animals practice finding food and staying safe before they go free.

news.headline: Radio Signals Heard From a Faraway Planet
news.body: For the first time, scientists have picked up radio waves coming from a single planet outside our Solar System. The giant world, called Beta Pictoris b, sits about 63 light years from Earth and is many times heavier than Jupiter. Researchers think the signals are linked to huge auroras — like Earth's Northern Lights — and that the planet's magnetic field is thousands of times stronger than ours.

news.headline: Meet Maggie Moo, the First Highland Calf
news.body: A wildlife park in England is celebrating its first Highland calf, born on October 1. The fluffy newcomer is named Maggie after her mom, Morag, and visitors already call her Maggie Moo. Keepers say she bonded with the herd within an hour and quickly became a star with park guests snapping photos at the fence.
